chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Asim from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in a will that a woman alone witnessed, that the testimony of a woman is accepted for one-quarter of the will.
ai.seo_question: How is a woman's testimony validated in Islamic inheritance law regarding wills?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) pragmatic legal reasoning in establishing the testimony of a single woman as valid for one-quarter of a will, a ruling that reflects the principle of *kaffat al-rijal* (one man equals four women) in specific financial contexts. It underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in adapting evidentiary standards to practical realities, distinguishing this partial validation from the full validity required for male testimony.
